newsitem.title: USA: AC-Pacific Intertie limited to 2,800 MW Tues -- BPA.
newsitem.headline: AC-Pacific Intertie limited to 2,800 MW Tues -- BPA.

text.p: North-to-south power transmissions on the AC segment of the Pacific Intertie are limited to 2,800 megawatts (MW) until 1800 PDT today/0100 GMT Wednesday, the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) confirmed today.
BPA, operator of the lines linking Northwest power plants to the California market, said Monday the restrictions were tentative.
The 4,800 MW-capacity AC line has been limited to 3,200 MW since a major power outage on Aug 10, and was scheduled to be limited to 2,000 MW on Monday and Tuesday.

But San Francisco-based Pacific Gas and Electric Co, citing high power demand due to an unseasonally late heat wave in California, decided Monday to delay maintenance work this week on its own section of the Intertie until the weekend.

The AC line restrictions will ease to 2,900 MW between 1800 and 2100 PDT on Tuesday, but will return to 2,800 MW between 0600 and 1800 PDT on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, again for maintenance work by PG&E.
Meanwhile, restrictions on the DC segment of the Intertie remain in place, with transmissions limited to around 1,080 MW through October 15.
The DC line has a capacity of 3,200 MW, but it had been capped at 2,000 MW since the Aug 10 outage.
